thread:
Aisha: quick ask for eng/runtime: we need validated bench numbers for the launch blog + the webinar. high level metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/s, end-to-end wall time, and GPU mem. sequences: 512, 2048, 8192. include cold vs warmed cache runs. target turnaround: 72h.

Ben: add request: note any kernel fallbacks and if kernel selection differs between int8/fp16. marketing will call out p95 + p99 in the narrative.

Sam: ok. want fp16 baseline + int8 quantized. do we need int4 too?

Aisha: int8 is enough for launch. int4 would be nice but optional. prioritize correctness + repeatability over extra configs.

Kai: plan: 1) smoke on small set today 2) full runs tomorrow. we'll do 3 cache states: cold (new process, empty KV), warmed (same session reuse), prefix-cached (shared common prompt prefix). we'll also log batch sizes, kernel ids, and per-step GPU utilization.

Ben: also include a tiny "real traffic" set (12 prompts) and a synthetic mix (200 prompts) so we can show both real and stress numbers in slides.

Aisha: i'll drop two files into marketing/bench_assets: `webinar_real_prompts.txt` (12) and `launch_synthetic_200.jsonl` (200). include a short description line per prompt. embargo: please mark outputs internal until we give go for publish.

Sam: can you confirm run CSV schema you want? i'm thinking: run_id, model, quant_mode, seq_len, cache_state, reps, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_s, gpu_mem_mb, batch_size, kernel_id, anomalies. any other?

Ben: add cost_est_usd_per_1m_tokens and notes field for transient errors.

Kai: example invocation (runs under /bench/runtime/marketing):
```
./bench_runner --model gpt-rlhf-1 --quant int8 --seq 2048 --prompts marketing/bench_assets/webinar_real_prompts.txt --cache prefix-cached --reps 300 --out /tmp/run_176907
```

Sam: we'll also fix RNG seed for synthetic to make results repeatable and include the exact docker image + commit. we'll snapshot kernel selection and any cudnn fallbacks.

ops-bot: infra note: high-seq jobs (>4k seq) may require a different instance type; @ops will watch for throttles.

deploy-bot: scheduled bench job 1769072001 by Sam (eng-runtime) 1queued	

Kai: please include raw logs (stdout/stderr), CSV summary, and a README.md that lists run commands, image tags, and known caveats. we'll flag runs with OOMs or retries in the anomalies column.

Aisha: deadline still 72h. ask: can we get the smoke CSV (small set) within 24h so marketing can draft the slides?

Sam: yes. smoke CSV by tomorrow morning. full annotated CSVs and logs by EOD in 72h. we'll try to include a short paragraph of caveats for the blog (kernel fallbacks may inflate p99 on 8k).

Ben: awesome. once we have p95/p99 we'll iterate messaging so we don't overclaim. thanks team. :rocket:
